justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: PatientManagementModule covers demographics (R-01), SchedulingModule with Redis Cache manages resource clashes (R-02), EMR Management Component with Audit & Compliance Container handles EMR audits (R-03), and BillingModule with Clearinghouse Adapter Component handles claims (R-04).
justifications.performance_efficiency: Sub-second EMR loads (R-07) are well-supported via Encrypted Redis Cache, Timeline Aggregator Component, and PgBouncer Connection Pooler. Asynchronous event streaming via Apache Kafka and analytical offloading to ClickHouse Database ensure high throughput.
justifications.compatibility: The Integration Service Container provides a dedicated FHIR Gateway Component using HAPI FHIR for lab and imaging integrations (R-08), alongside the Clearinghouse Adapter Component utilizing X12 EDI for insurance clearinghouses.
justifications.usability: The Frontend Container provides dedicated Clinical & Administrative Feature Modules for all defined roles (Clinician, Patient, Staff, Billing). The Notification Container provides multi-channel alerting (SMS, email, push), though specific native mobile delivery mechanisms are not detailed.
justifications.reliability: Patroni & Etcd Replication & HA Controller, Outbox & Retry Dispatcher, and Kafka KRaft Quorum provide high availability. However, true cross-region active-active data conflict resolution across on-prem-k8s and eu-central-1 is not fully elaborated.
justifications.security: Addresses R-05, HIPAA, and GDPR thoroughly: Authentication & Authorization Filter enforces OIDC MFA and OPA; pgcrypto Encryption Module ensures AES-256 at rest; and Audit & Compliance Container provides hash-validated retention.
justifications.maintainability: High modularity with decoupled containers (EMR Service, Core Services, Integration Service) communicating over Kafka and Istio mTLS. However, component diagrams blur container boundaries by listing neighboring containers as internal components.
justifications.portability: The system utilizes standard containerized stacks (Go, Spring Boot, React) managed by Istio Service Mesh, suitable for hybrid deployment across on-prem-k8s and AWS eu-central-1, though cloud abstraction abstractions for storage are minimal.

PERF-01.justification: The EMR Service uses a Go-based Timeline Aggregator backed by an Encrypted Redis Cache and PgBouncer connection pooling, ensuring P95 query latencies stay well below 1 second under 500 concurrent clinician requests.
sensitivity_points: Cache hit ratio on Timeline Aggregator
PgBouncer connection pool sizing under burst load
tradeoffs: Memory overhead for timeline caching versus sub-second retrieval latency

PERF-02.justification: Ingestion traffic is handled via the dedicated FHIR Gateway, Camel transformation engine, and Kafka buffering, isolating high write volumes from clinician reads; however, the consumer pipeline into EMR storage is partially implicit.
sensitivity_points: Kafka partition parallelism for HL7 ingestion
PostgreSQL write throughput during batch ingestion bursts
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency of lab results in EMR versus query performance isolation

AVAIL-01.justification: Patroni and Etcd provide automated failover with synchronous replication to prevent data loss, but cross-site global load balancing and WAN latency impacts for active-active hybrid routing are not explicitly defined.
sensitivity_points: Cross-site network latency for Etcd consensus and synchronous replication
Global DNS or load balancer health-check and failover convergence time
tradeoffs: Synchronous replication prevents data loss but increases write latency across WAN

AVAIL-02.justification: The Outbox & Retry Dispatcher combined with Patroni and Etcd automated database failover within 30 seconds ensures transactional integrity and safe idempotency retries for claims without duplicate submission.
sensitivity_points: Outbox retry idempotency keys sent to clearinghouses
tradeoffs: Transactional outbox table storage overhead versus guaranteed at-least-once message delivery

MOD-01.justification: The dedicated Clearinghouse Adapter Component and Apache Camel transformation engine isolate external partner interfaces within the Integration Service, ensuring EMR and Core services remain completely untouched.
sensitivity_points: Extensibility of Apache Camel transformation engine
tradeoffs: Generic adapter abstraction complexity versus isolated clearinghouse modifications

MOD-02.justification: The change cleanly maps to the Frontend feature module, the Core Services PatientManagementModule, and PostgreSQL tables with pgaudit. Three components are affected, though schema evolution across partitioned tables adds minor operational overhead.
sensitivity_points: Schema migration tooling for partitioned demographic tables
Coupling between UI forms and backend demographic models
tradeoffs: Automated database-level pgaudit capturing versus custom demographic event serialization

SEC-01.justification: The external IdP and API Gateway Authentication Filter strictly enforce MFA and reject password-only access. Kafka and the Audit container log the attempt, though automated real-time SIEM alerting within one minute relies on external or generalized notification paths.
sensitivity_points: MFA enforcement token validation latency at API Gateway
Alert processing delay across Kafka stream ingestion
tradeoffs: Strict mandatory MFA versus clinician friction during emergency workflow overrides

SEC-02.justification: The Access Control Enforcer validates clinical relationship policies, while pgaudit and Kafka capture read events. The Audit & Compliance Container indexes them into ClickHouse and archives with SHA-256 hashes to object storage, fulfilling 10-year tamper-evident retention.
sensitivity_points: Policy evaluation overhead in Access Control Enforcer on every read
Immutability verification of cold storage archives with SHA-256
tradeoffs: Performance cost of auditing every EMR read versus absolute compliance guarantee
